title: Integrate differential-drive odometry
scope: Exact constant-wheel arc on a planar model

items.prompt: A delivery cart starts at the origin with heading 0 (heading is measured counter-clockwise from +x, so a left turn makes y positive). Its left and right wheels roll at constant linear speeds vl=0.2 m/s and vr=0.6 m/s, track width b=0.4 m, for t=1 s, without slip. Integrate this constant-speed motion exactly and return the final x, y and heading. Give positions to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m); the heading is graded within ±0.001 rad and any angle equivalent modulo 2π is accepted.
items.solution: v = (0.2+0.6)/2 = 0.4 m/s, ω = (0.6-0.2)/0.4 = 1 rad/s, ωt = 1 rad. x = 0.4·sin(1)/1 = 0.336588 m, y = 0.4·(1-cos(1))/1 = 0.183879 m, heading = 1 rad. A single Euler step would give (0.4, 0) and a midpoint step (0.351, 0.192); both miss the exact arc by more than 0.001 m. This is odometry from wheel speeds, not localization.
hints: The right wheel is faster, so the cart curves left (counter-clockwise): expect y > 0 and a final heading of about 1 rad.
v = (vl+vr)/2 = 0.4 m/s and ω = (vr-vl)/b = 1 rad/s. Next evaluate the exact arc from the origin with t = 1 s: x = v·sin(ωt)/ω, y = v·(1-cos(ωt))/ω, heading = ωt (angles in radians).

v = (0.2+0.6)/2 = 0.4 m/s, ω = (0.6-0.2)/0.4 = 1 rad/s, ωt = 1 rad. x = 0.4·sin(1)/1 = 0.336588 m, y = 0.4·(1-cos(1))/1 = 0.183879 m, heading = 1 rad. A single Euler step would give (0.4, 0) and a midpoint step (0.351, 0.192); both miss the exact arc by more than 0.001 m. This is odometry from wheel speeds, not localization.
items.remediation: If you got about (0.4, 0) you took one Euler step along the initial heading; about (0.351, 0.192) means a midpoint (RK2) step. Both approximate the arc. If y has the wrong sign, check ω = (vr-vl)/b. Revisit /lessons/R02.

A single Euler step would give (-0.25, 0) and a midpoint step (0.104, -0.227); both miss the exact arc by more than 0.001 m. This is odometry from wheel speeds, not localization.

items.prompt: An inspection rover starts at world pose x=1.5 m, y=-0.5 m, heading 0.5 rad (counter-clockwise from world +x). Its wheels roll at constant linear speeds vl=0.1 m/s and vr=0.3 m/s, track width b=0.4 m, for t=2 s, without slip. Integrate the constant wheel speeds exactly and return the final world x, y and heading. Give positions to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m); the heading is graded within ±0.001 rad and any angle equivalent modulo 2π is accepted.
items.solution: v = (0.1+0.3)/2 = 0.2 m/s, ω = (0.3-0.1)/0.4 = 0.5 rad/s, ωt = 1 rad. Body arc: dx = 0.336588 m, dy = 0.183879 m. World: x = 1.5 + cos(0.5)·dx - sin(0.5)·dy = 1.707228 m, y = -0.5 + sin(0.5)·dx + cos(0.5)·dy = -0.177262 m, heading = 1.5 rad. An Euler step would give (1.851, -0.308) and a midpoint step (1.716, -0.163); both miss by more than 0.001 m.
hints: The rover curves left by 1 rad while starting at heading 0.5 rad, so its body-frame arc must be turned by 0.5 rad before it is added to the start position.
v = 0.2 m/s and ω = 0.5 rad/s. Body-frame arc over t = 2 s: dx = v·sin(ωt)/ω, dy = v·(1-cos(ωt))/ω. Next rotate (dx, dy) by the initial heading 0.5 rad and add (1.5, -0.5).

v = (0.1+0.3)/2 = 0.2 m/s, ω = (0.3-0.1)/0.4 = 0.5 rad/s, ωt = 1 rad. Body arc: dx = 0.336588 m, dy = 0.183879 m. World: x = 1.5 + cos(0.5)·dx - sin(0.5)·dy = 1.707228 m, y = -0.5 + sin(0.5)·dx + cos(0.5)·dy = -0.177262 m, heading = 1.5 rad. An Euler step would give (1.851, -0.308) and a midpoint step (1.716, -0.163); both miss by more than 0.001 m.
items.remediation: If you got about (1.837, -0.316) you added the body-frame arc without rotating it by the initial heading. About (1.851, -0.308) is one Euler step and (1.716, -0.163) a midpoint step; use the exact arc. Revisit /lessons/R02.

items.prompt: An inspection rover starts at world pose x=1 m, y=-1 m, heading 0.7 rad (counter-clockwise from world +x). Its wheels roll at constant linear speeds vl=-0.1 m/s and vr=0.3 m/s, track width b=0.4 m, for t=2 s, without slip. Integrate the constant wheel speeds exactly and return the final world x, y and heading. Give positions to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m); the heading is graded within ±0.001 rad and any angle equivalent modulo 2π is accepted.
items.solution: v = (-0.1+0.3)/2 = 0.1 m/s, ω = (0.3-(-0.1))/0.4 = 1 rad/s, ωt = 2 rad: a tight left turn with one wheel reversing. Body arc: dx = v·sin(ωt)/ω = 0.090930 m, dy = v·(1-cos(ωt))/ω = 0.141615 m. World: x = 1 + cos(0.7)·dx - sin(0.7)·dy = 0.978316 m, y = -1 + sin(0.7)·dx + cos(0.7)·dy = -0.833109 m, heading = 0.7 + 2 = 2.7 rad. An Euler step would give (1.153, -0.871) and a midpoint step (0.974, -0.802); both miss by more than 0.001 m.
hints: One wheel runs backwards, so the rover turns sharply while creeping forward; the turn is large, so a straight-line step will not do.
Compute v = (vl+vr)/2 and ω = (vr-vl)/b, form the body-frame arc dx = v·sin(ωt)/ω, dy = v·(1-cos(ωt))/ω, then rotate it by the start heading before adding the start position.

World: x = 1 + cos(0.7)·dx - sin(0.7)·dy = 0.978316 m, y = -1 + sin(0.7)·dx + cos(0.7)·dy = -0.833109 m, heading = 0.7 + 2 = 2.7 rad. An Euler step would give (1.153, -0.871) and a midpoint step (0.974, -0.802); both miss by more than 0.001 m.
items.remediation: About (1.153, -0.871) is one Euler step and (0.974, -0.802) a midpoint step; (1.091, -0.858) means the arc was added without rotating it by the start heading 0.7 rad. Revisit /lessons/R02.

items.solution: v = (-0.15+(-0.45))/2 = -0.3 m/s, ω = (-0.45-(-0.15))/0.5 = -0.6 rad/s, ωt = -1.8 rad. Body arc: dx = -0.486924 m, dy = 0.613601 m.
